questions.question: What is a GitHub Issue best used for?

options.B: Tracking actionable tasks, bug reports, feature requests, and technical debt in a repository

questions.explanation: Issues are actionable tickets representing concrete bugs or features to be implemented.

questions.question: When should a team use GitHub Discussions instead of GitHub Issues?

options.A: When they want to delete code
options.B: For open-ended questions, community Q&A, brainstorming ideas, and general announcements that are not yet actionable tasks
options.C: Only when the repository is private

questions.explanation: Discussions provide an open forum format for community Q&A and ideas without cluttering the actionable issue backlog.

questions.question: Which keyword in a Pull Request description will automatically close Issue #42 when the PR is merged into default branch?
questions.explanation: `Closes #42`, `Fixes #42`, or `Resolves #42` instructs GitHub to mark Issue #42 as closed upon merging.

questions.question: What are GitHub Issue Labels (e.g. `bug`, `enhancement`, `good first issue`) used for?

options.A: To categorize, prioritize, and filter issues and pull requests across a project
options.B: To change the repository font color
options.C: To charge users for creating tickets
options.D: To restrict who can read the repository

questions.explanation: Labels categorize tickets, making it easy to filter by topic, difficulty, or urgency.

questions.question: What does the label `good first issue` typically signal on GitHub?

options.A: An issue that only senior engineers are allowed to fix
options.B: A beginner-friendly task with low complexity curated specifically for newcomers to make their first contribution
options.C: The first issue ever created in the repo history
options.D: An issue with a monetary bounty

questions.explanation: `good first issue` is an open-source standard helping students and new contributors find accessible introductory tasks.

questions.question: What is the recommended chronological order of the 'GitHub Flow' in team projects?

options.B: Issue/Task → Feature Branch → Commits → Pull Request → Code Review → Merge to Main
options.C: Merge to Main → Branch → Issue → Test

questions.explanation: GitHub Flow is the industry-standard lightweight workflow: define task, branch, code, PR, review, and merge.

questions.question: How do you mention a teammate in an issue or PR comment to notify them?
questions.explanation: Prefixing a username with `@` (e.g. `@alice`) pings that user and sends a notification.

questions.question: What is a GitHub Project Board (Kanban board)?

options.A: A visual spreadsheet of columns (e.g. Todo, In Progress, Done) to manage workflow cards across team members

questions.explanation: GitHub Projects provide Kanban boards to track sprint progress and task status visually.

questions.question: What is an Issue Template?

options.A: A pre-formatted markdown template prompting reporters for specific details (like steps to reproduce, expected behavior, screenshots)
options.B: A script that writes code automatically

questions.explanation: Issue templates guide users to submit complete, reproducible bug reports rather than vague complaints.

questions.question: Why should teams avoid using WhatsApp or DMs for technical task tracking during a hackathon?

options.A: WhatsApp messages cannot be searched or linked to commits, PRs, and code history
options.B: GitHub charges extra if you use chat apps
options.C: Git commands fail if WhatsApp is open
options.D: Because coding is only allowed in silence

questions.explanation: Tracking tasks in GitHub Issues preserves context, assigns responsibility, links directly to PRs, and keeps everyone aligned.
